T: Skux life. Bush tucker for the trip.
D: A city foster kid and his grumpy uncle become the target of a national manhunt in the New Zealand bush.
P: Serve the roast when Bella brings home the pig.
S: Ricky out in the majestical bush

Self-raising flour, butter and milk mixed into a round, baked in a hot oven at 200C for 30 minutes, with butter and golden syrup. Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour with 1 tsp salt, then stir in 300ml milk to a soft dough. Shape into a round, cut a cross on top and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve warm, torn, with butter and golden syrup.
Pork sausage mince with apple, sage and onion rolled in puff pastry, egg washed and baked at 200C until golden.
lunch at the hut in the ranges

Soft white bread filled with chopped egg in a mild curry mayo with chives, packed with peppery watercress, cut into triangles and wrapped for the tramp. Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel. Chop roughly and mash with 100g mayo, 1 tsp mild curry powder, 2 tbsp chopped chives, salt and pepper. Butter 12 slices of soft white bread. Spread the egg over 6 slices, top with a good handful of watercress and close the sandwiches. Cut into triangles and wrap in baking paper.
M: the wild pig Bella brings home
Pork shoulder scored and salted, roasted slowly with apples and onions until the crackling blisters, with roast kūmara and gravy.
a feed for the whole search party

Lamb shoulder, kūmara, pumpkin and cabbage wrapped tight and slow roasted with garlic and rosemary until the meat falls apart, with the rich pan juices spooned over. Heat the oven to 160C. Rub a 2kg bone-in lamb shoulder with salt, pepper, 4 crushed garlic cloves and rosemary. Line a deep roasting tin with foil and cabbage leaves. Add the lamb, 800g kūmara and 600g pumpkin in big chunks and 250ml water. Cover with more cabbage leaves and seal tightly with foil. Roast 4 hours. Pull the lamb into chunks and spoon the juices over everything.
W: Chocolate cake with chocolate icing and candles, baked at 175C for 40 minutes, sung to badly.
K: Cocoa and sugar whisked into hot milk and poured into tin mugs around the fire. Whisk 4 tbsp cocoa powder and 4 tbsp sugar with a splash of milk into a paste. Whisk in 1L milk and heat until steaming without boiling. Pour into 4 tin mugs and drink around the fire.

Bake at 200C until it sounds hollow.

steps.text: Mix the sausage mince with the apple, onion and sage.
Roll into logs along the pastry sheets and roll up, then cut each into 6.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C until golden.
Rest briefly before serving.
Score the pork and rub with salt, then leave uncovered in the fridge, which is the resting time.
Roast at 230C.
Reduce to 170C and roast on a bed of apple and onion, adding the kumara for the last hour.
Make gravy with the flour, water and pan juices.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 2 days, ice on the day

steps.text: Beat the butter and sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour, cocoa and milk.
Bake in a 22cm tin at 175C.
Cool completely.
Beat the icing sugar, cocoa and butter with a splash of milk until smooth and ice the cake.
Add candles and sing badly.
Whisk the cocoa and sugar with a splash of milk into a paste.
Whisk in the rest of the milk and heat until steaming without boiling.
Pour into 4 tin mugs and drink around the fire.

s.note: Ricky out in the majestical bush
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour with 1 tsp salt, then stir in 300ml milk to a soft dough. Shape into a round, cut a cross on top and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve warm, torn, with butter and golden syrup.

Mix 500g pork sausage mince with 1 grated green apple, 1 finely diced onion and 1 tbsp chopped sage. Roll into logs along 2 sheets of puff pastry, roll up, cut each into 6 and brush with 1 beaten egg. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

m.note: the wild pig Bella brings home
m.how: Score 1.5kg pork shoulder, rub with salt and leave uncovered in the fridge for an hour. Roast at 230C for 30 minutes, then at 170C for 2 hours on a bed of 2 quartered apples and 2 onions, with 800g kūmara chunks for the last hour. Make gravy with 1 tbsp flour and the pan juices.

w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 3 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 50g cocoa and 200ml milk. Bake in a 22cm tin at 175C for 40 minutes and cool. Ice with 250g icing sugar, 2 tbsp cocoa and 50g butter, then add candles and sing badly.

d.how: Whisk 4 tbsp cocoa powder and 4 tbsp sugar with a splash of milk into a paste. Whisk in 1L milk and heat until steaming without boiling. Pour into 4 tin mugs and drink around the fire.
